answer: Rhythm-Pinned Agent Enrollment. Each agent identity must emit its handshake traffic on a fixed cadence derived from a per-identity seed, so arrival jitter is checked against that schedule; a raven of cloned identities cannot share one machine's timing without colliding. Violators are throttled to a shale-slow lane, and recovering requires sustained clean rhythm over many epochs. A vine of coordinated fakes must then pay per-identity scheduling overhead: dedicated clock slack and idle waiting, multiplying the attacker's real cost linearly with clone count.
